entries.reason: Pass 1: 'the first word' asserts that the headword is the first word shown. That holds on the 15 bare-card carriers, whose prompt says 'the word on the card'. It fails on the 14 sentence carriers, whose prompt says 'the word in capitals', because the capitalised word is not the first word of the sentence. A child there may look up the wrong word. misfiledCarriers.why: For HUGE, 'heavy' is a property huge things often have, not a tilt of its meaning. This is vr04-one-feature-only, and that entry already carries 'tall' on the same item.
For TRANSPARENT, 'thin' is a physical reason something can be see-through, not a near-meaning with a different slant. It is closer to one-feature-only.
A MELANCHOLY tune is often gentle, but 'gentle' does not share sadness's area of meaning. It co-occurs rather than shades, which makes it vr04-keeps-the-same-company.

This option runs in the wrong direction or does not change at all: a peek is no longer or stronger than a glance, while whisper to shout gets stronger.
'Content' is no stronger than 'pleased' and arguably milder, so the change is zero or reversed, not too small.
